messages:
monitor-bot: ALERT: us-west2 GPU capacity -18% over last 12m. Spike in Xid and CE counts on racks r3-r6. Auto-drain triggered for 24 GPUs. See CI:alert/1749998888

maya: seeing same, dashboards show nvSwitch probe latency jump ~10x before drains. Noting probes timeout -> nodes marked unhealthy -> autoscaler evacs.

sanjay: can you paste the probe logs? wondering if telemetry delay is upstream (eg: ntd agent backlog) or actual fabric flaps.

ella: grabbing logs now. quick grep:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:02Z] nv_switch_probe: latency=2.1s status=ok
[2026-03-18T09:12:05Z] nv_switch_probe: latency=2.5s status=warn
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] nv_switch_probe: timeout error
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] gpu_card[slot-7]: Xid 31 count++
[2026-03-18T09:12:11Z] gpu_card[slot-7]: correctable_ecc++
```

chris: that's consistent with a probe timeout leading to soft-ecc inflation and Xid 31. I've seen firmware 51.3.x earlier cause similar timings. Any recent firmware churn in us-west2?

lee: ops-bot reports a firmware recompute job pushed 51.3.4 -> 51.4.0 ~3h ago to racks r3-r5 (rolling). Could correlate.

maya: ok, plan suggestion: 1) pause auto-drain policy for 10m for impacted ASGs (to avoid mass eviction cascade), 2) throttle probe frequency/raise probe timeout to 5s, 3) roll back firmware on a canary node if we can reproduce. Thoughts? :thinking:

katie: +1 to temporarily pausing drains, but we need manual guardrails so we don't leave genuinely bad cards online. Maybe change action from drain->mark-degraded so scheduler stops new allocations but keeps existing workloads until manual triage.

monitor-bot: ACTION_LOG: auto-drain paused on asg-usw2-gpu-a for 10m by maya.

ella: I'm running a one-off probe reconfig on r3 to increase timeout. Will push change to r4-r6 if metrics stabilize.

chris: I'll open a quick firmware-rollback RFC for r3 canary and coordinate with build team. If rollback reduces probe latency and Xid counts -> we should roll further.

sanjay: also, network fabric controller had a backlog earlier (netctrl queue depth spike around 09:09). Could be causing nvswitch manager API slowness. Putting Eng-Net on a page.

lee: paging @eng-network oncall.

eng-network-bot: Page sent to oncall-networking: paged kieran. Response ETA ~7m.

maya: short-term capacity asks: can we borrow 12 gpus from eu-west1 spare pool to relieve pressure on scheduling? We'll shift some batch workloads. Cost tradeoff: cross-region spill adds egress + latency for some workloads, but preserves PL customer latency SLOs.

katie: finance note: emergency inter-region spill will be charged at overprovision rates; if we exceed reserved commit >15% this month ops will need exec approval. Can we limit to non-SL SLO tenants only?

maya: yes, only shift non-prod/batch for now. Customers with latency SLOs remain pinned.

ella: update after tweak: probe latency dropped to ~210ms on r3 after timeout bump and netctrl queue drained. Xid rate on slot-7 dropped from 6/min -> 0.2/min over 8m.

chris: nice. hold off rollback for now until we confirm trend over 30m. If number creeps back up we'll rollback.

sanjay: writing quick detection rule: if nv_switch_probe latency >1s AND Xid_rate >3/min for >5m, create high-priority incident and auto-throttle probe frequency. This avoids cascade triggers.

maya: agree. Also file a follow-up postmortem to look at: probe sensitivity, firmware rollout gating, and autoscaler hysteresis (we drained too fast).

monitor-bot: NOTE: 12 GPUs borrowed from eu-west1 spare pool initiated at 09:25 UTC (spill id spill-1749998888-eu).

chris: postmortem owners: maya (lead), sanjay (detection), chris (firmware), lee (autoscaler changes). I'll create the doc.

katie: finance loop: I'll pre-approve one-time spill up to $3k for this event, but log all charges.

eng-network-bot: oncall kieran: netctrl backlog traced to a faulty NIC firmware on mgmt-switch-21. Replacing NIC now.

ella: after NIC swap, nv_switch_probe steady ~90-150ms, no Xid increases in last 12m. Re-enabling normal auto-drain policy at 09:36.

maya: re-enable confirmed. Closing immediate alert; leaving the spill active for 1h to smooth scheduling.

monitor-bot: ALERT_RESOLVED: us-west2 GPU capacity restored to -2% within 30m. Event closed, follow-up PT scheduled.

chris: thumbs up. Learned: don't rely on aggressive probe->drain mapping during mass firmware churn. Tune probe timeouts and give network controller backpressure handling.

katie: will track cost and ping exec if we hit reserve thresholds.

maya: thanks all :heart: — will post postmortem draft in #postmortems in ~2d.
